channel.title: Commandline on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Commandline on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: commandline: Designing product simplicity for the AI era
item.description:
The article asks whether shared design components are sufficient for a seamless product experience, or whether designers need to prioritize simplicity over complexity to create consistency. It frames this as a product design question for the AI era.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Your agent’s guardrails have a bypass
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Agent Hooks, an open, framework-neutral governance contract for agent systems. It includes conformance testing and is intended to make enforcement fail closed instead of failing open when controls crash.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: One requirement, many failure paths: Evaluate, control, and optimize with ASSERT and ACS
item.description:
The article says a safety requirement can have a complex runtime failure surface even when it seems simple. It highlights ASSERT for finding coverage bugs and ACS for fixing the policy.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Stop restricting the agent. Start restricting its environment.
item.description:
Azure SRE Agent argues that AI safety is better achieved by constraining the runtime environment rather than the agent itself. This approach aims to preserve autonomy while reducing risk compared with human review or standing credentials.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: How we built ThinkingBox to measure whether agents finish the job
item.description:
ThinkingBox splits the execution framework from the benchmark package so each can be updated independently. The article frames this as a way to measure whether agents actually finish tasks.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Watch TypeScript creator Anders Hejlsberg on The Peterman Pod
item.description:
After TypeScript 7.0, Anders Hejlsberg discusses porting TypeScript from JavaScript to Go, along with the benefits and drawbacks of agentic AI for coding. The post is a podcast announcement rather than a technical changelog.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Who spent all the tokens? Real-time, run-scoped cost control for AI agents
item.description:
TokenOps is presented as a run-scoped cost control mechanism for AI agents that enforces a shared budget in real time. The stated goal is to stop runaway runs before costs accumulate and invoices arrive.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: 🌿 Agent Terrarium: Bringing AI agents to life
item.description:
A weekend open-source desktop companion app, Agent Terrarium, explores a more interactive, less purely transactional way to work with AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Tool search: Finding the right tool at the right time
item.description:
The article says the value in adding more tools to AI agents comes from surfacing the right tool at the right time, instead of exposing every tool upfront. It focuses on discoverability as the key problem.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: From research to reality: An interview with Microsoft VP of Security Research Taesoo Kim
item.description:
Microsoft interviewed Taesoo Kim, VP of Security Research and head of Security FORGE Labs, about codename MDASH and the lab’s work on security research. The interview highlights a multi-model, agentic approach as a potential direction for improving security capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: A wind farm you can talk to: Building a real-time 3D digital twin on Microsoft Fabric
item.description:
The article describes building a real-time 3D digital twin for a wind farm on Microsoft Fabric by combining geometry, telemetry, and language in one simulation. It emphasizes using the model to spend more time on architectural decisions.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: How my dev machine built 1,111 word-processing features and forgot to add a ruler
item.description:
The piece describes an experiment where a complex agentic AI loop was used to build an online collaborative word processor, reflecting on the results and what emerged from letting the system run mostly on its own. The title suggests the system produced many features but still missed basic editor functionality like a ruler.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Where the agent decides, and where the tools actually run
item.description:
The article frames a design question about where to place an agent’s decision-making logic in an application that already has a deterministic state machine, tool integrations, and CI/CD. It focuses on separating the “brain” (judgment) from the “hands” (tool execution) within a graph/state-based architecture.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: The durable asset is the loop you own. OpenEnv is its protocol.
item.description:
The article argues that the durable asset in agentic AI is the learning loop, not the rented model, and presents OpenEnv as the protocol for reinforcement learning environments. It positions OpenEnv around owning and standardizing the environment/evaluation loop for recursive self-improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Introducing the Agentic Resource Discovery specification
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification, an open standard for AI clients to automatically find resources relevant to a task. It was developed with partners including GoDaddy, Google, and Hugging Face.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Information-flow control: Moving toward secure, autonomous agents
item.description:
The article says information-flow control (IFC) is a deterministic security approach that could help make autonomous agents more secure. It presents IFC as a path toward controlling how information moves through agent systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog
